machine learning: the field where computers learn patterns from data instead of being told rules
main course: the largest part of a meal, served after the starter
make a decision: to choose what to do after thinking about it
make breakfast: to prepare the first meal of the day
make the bed: to pull the sheets and covers straight on a bed
make up: to become friends again after an argument, or to invent something
market share: the part of all sales in a market that one company holds
may well: used to say something is quite likely
meet a deadline: to finish work by the agreed time
meet halfway: for two sides to each accept part of what the other wants
mental health: the state of your mind and feelings
miss a flight: to arrive too late for a plane you booked
miss the boat: to lose a chance by being too slow
missed call: a phone call that was not answered
mistake / error / fault: something done wrongly, or the cause of it
mop the floor: to clean the floor with water and a mop
movie theater: a building where films are shown on a big screen
natural resources: materials such as water, wood and oil taken from the earth
need / require / demand: to call for something, by necessity, by rule, or by force
neural network: a computing system loosely modelled on the brain's connected cells
next to: beside something, with nothing in between
no pain, no gain: you cannot succeed without effort and difficulty
normal / ordinary / typical: usual, with nothing special about it
not my cup of tea: not the kind of thing I enjoy
notice period: the time you must work after saying you will leave a job
notification sound: the short sound a phone makes for a new message
on the ball: quick to notice things and act well
on the same page: in agreement about what is happening or planned
on thin ice: in a risky position where you could easily get into trouble
on time: at the planned time, not late
onboarding: the process of bringing a new employee into a company
open source: with code that anyone may read, use and change
ozone layer: the band of gas high in the air that blocks harmful sunlight
paint a rosy picture: to describe something as better than it really is
paint town red: to go out and celebrate wildly
passport control: the airport desk where officials check your passport
pay a bill: to give the money owed for something
pay a visit: to go and see someone or somewhere
pay attention: to watch or listen with care
peas: small round green seeds eaten as a vegetable
peer review: the checking of research by other experts in the same field
pick out: to choose or recognize one thing among others
pick up: to lift something, collect someone, or learn something casually
place an order: to ask a shop or company to send you goods
place emphasis on: to give special importance to something
police car: the vehicle police officers drive on duty
police officer: a member of the police force
police station: the local office and base of the police
post office: the place where you send letters and parcels
preheat the oven: to heat the oven before putting food in it
prescription drug: a medicine you may only get with a doctor's order
press release: an official statement given to journalists
price tag: the label showing what something costs
problem / issue / dilemma: a difficulty, a matter to discuss, or a hard choice
pull no punches: to speak honestly and harshly, holding nothing back
pull yourself together: to control your feelings and start acting calmly
pull yourself up: to lift yourself back to your feet or your position
put forward: to suggest an idea or a name for others to consider
put off: to delay something, or to make someone lose interest
put up: to build something, or to let someone stay in your home
put up with: to accept something annoying without complaining
